headline: GR SILVER BREAKS 150m PAST RESOURCE BOUNDARY AT SAN MARCIAL — 21.9m AT 168 g/t Ag IN SE EXTENSION (TSXV:GRSL)
snippet: GR Silver Mining (TSXV: GRSL) announced July 10 that hole SMS26-07 at the San Marcial deposit in Mexico's Plomosas Project returned 21.9 metres at 168 g/t Ag, including 6.15 metres at 447 g/t Ag in the SE Extension target — confirming that high-grade silver mineralization continues for at least an additional 150 metres to the southeast of the 2023 NI 43-101 Mineral Resource Estimate boundary. This result validates GR Silver's resource expansion thesis: it is the same breccia-controlled structural corridor that produced the best-ever SMS26-04 (45.1m at 1,623 g/t Ag in May) now confirmed to extend beyond all existing resource limits, at a silver price above $59/oz that makes every additional metre of proven strike length directly accretive to NAV. With the 2023 MRE already established and the SE Extension open to further drilling, the next resource update could materially re-rate the deposit.

headline: PILBARA GOLD STARTS 12,000m RC AT ROE HILLS — FIRST DRILL IN 8 YEARS ON 1.8KM KALGOORLIE GOLD CORRIDOR (ASX:PGL)
source_name: Proactive Investors Australia / Pilbara Gold Ltd.
snippet: Pilbara Gold (ASX: PGL) announced this week that reverse circulation drilling has commenced at its Roe Hills Gold Project near Kalgoorlie, Western Australia, targeting a 1.8-kilometre bedrock gold corridor at the Terra and Caliburn prospects — the first systematic drilling at either target in eight years — with up to 12,000 metres planned over approximately 2.5 months and a maiden resource estimate targeted for late 2026 or early 2027. Prior drilling at Terra defined over 1,500 metres of strike and returned intersections including 35m at 1.00 g/t Au from 116.5m and 23m at 1.43 g/t Au from 104m, which at $4,100 gold and within trucking distance of established Kalgoorlie processing infrastructure provides the economic rationale for a systematic resource definition program. Roe Hills sits adjacent to Pilbara's flagship Mt York project, where a sixth drill rig was recently added — indicating management is building toward a consolidated multi-project resource base in the Western Australian Goldfields.

headline: G MINING TOCANTINZINHO: 36,845 OZ Q2 (+16% QoQ), RECORD STRIP — GRADE JUMP EXPECTED IN H2 (TSX:GMIN)
snippet: G Mining Ventures (TSX: GMIN, OTCQX: GMINF) reported July 9 that its Tocantinzinho Gold Mine in Pará State, Brazil produced 36,845 ounces in Q2 2026 — a 16% increase over Q1 — with a record quarterly mining rate of 6.3 million tonnes mined, putting H1 2026 at 68,691 oz and keeping full-year 2026 guidance of 160,000–190,000 oz intact. The critical detail is forward-looking: Phase 2 higher-grade mineralization is now accessible following the record strip campaign, and management guided for 'a significant increase in grade and production during the second half of 2026 allowing for substantially lower costs.' For GMIN investors, Q2 itself is solid but the thesis is the coming H2 grade inflection — a production re-rate into a $4,100 gold environment that should compress the cash cost curve significantly and expand margins from a mine that was less than three years from construction start to commercial production.

headline: ISOENERGY BACK DRILLING AFTER WILDFIRE — 4/4 PRE-SUSPENSION HOLES HIT URANIUM AT HURRICANE SOUTH (TSX:ISO)
snippet: IsoEnergy (TSX: ISO) announced July 8 that summer drilling at the Larocque East project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin has resumed following a precautionary evacuation triggered by nearby wildfires — with the company reporting that all four holes completed before the suspension intersected uranium mineralization, including a peak radioactivity reading of 43,160 counts per second over 0.5 metres on the Hurricane South Trend, confirming continuity of the newly identified L Fault Zone. Hurricane already hosts 48.6 million pounds U3O8 at 34.5% Indicated — the highest average grade of any uranium resource globally — and the summer's 8,000-metre program targeting up to 20 holes is specifically designed to extend the South Trend, which winter 2026 drilling confirmed extends 525 metres east of the current resource boundary. With 100% of pre-suspension holes returning mineralization and peak radioactivity above 43,000 cps, the geological model is executing as predicted.

headline: NORTHWEST COPPER DRILLS KWANIKA WITH 3 RIGS — 10,000m TO SUPPORT UPCOMING PEA ON BC COPPER-GOLD PORPHYRY (TSXV:NWST)
snippet: NorthWest Copper (TSXV: NWST) announced July 8 that three drill rigs are operating at the 100%-owned Kwanika copper-gold porphyry in north-central British Columbia, targeting up to 10,000 metres across 41 planned holes — 14 holes in the Western Zone (underground expansion) and 27 holes in the Pit Zone (near-surface infill and northern expansion) — with assay results expected later in summer and a Preliminary Economic Assessment to follow. Prior Kwanika drill highlights include 58 metres at 0.96% Cu and 1.04 g/t Au from 94 metres, and the 2026 program is specifically designed to upgrade Inferred tonnes to Indicated, widen the pit envelope to the north, and add underground ounces in the Western Zone — the three inputs needed to support a credible PEA. The company is also assessing options to extend drilling into fall. At $6.24/lb copper and $4,100 gold, a fully funded BC porphyry with a PEA pathway is well-positioned for institutional re-rating.

headline: INZINC WRAPS SPRING DRILLING AT B-9 APEX — GALLIUM-BEARING INDY SEDEX AWAITS ASSAYS FROM CENTRAL BC (TSXV:IZN)
snippet: InZinc Mining (TSXV: IZN) announced completion of its spring 2026 diamond drill program at the 100%-owned Indy Sedex (zinc-lead-silver-gallium-barite) project in central British Columbia, with core analysis now underway and assay results pending from the B-9 Apex Discovery — the most recently drill-confirmed target on a property covering stratigraphy and structures highly favourable for stratiform base metal mineralization. Indy's gallium-bearing character sets it apart from standard zinc-lead-silver sedex projects: gallium is a U.S.-designated critical mineral under active government strategic stockpiling, and an economic gallium credit could materially improve project economics and attract interest beyond the conventional base metals investment community. The pending B-9 Apex assays are the first results from this newly identified zone — watch for anomalous zinc, lead, silver, and gallium values that would confirm a new discovery on an underexplored but drill-permitted BC property.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,134 HEADING INTO MAKE-OR-BREAK CPI ON JULY 14 — FOMC SPLIT 9-8 PUTS SEPT HIKE ON A KNIFE'S EDGE
snippet: Gold is trading at $4,134 heading into a pivotal week as the June Consumer Price Index releases Monday July 14 at 8:30 AM ET — the single most consequential near-term catalyst for precious metals given the recently released FOMC minutes revealing a 9-to-8 committee split on a September rate hike. May CPI printed 4.2% year-over-year, directly triggering the hawkish dot-plot shift that erased the rally from $3,200 (October 2025) through $5,300 (January 2026); if June holds at or above 4.0%, September hike probability pushes toward 65% and real yields remain elevated, extending pressure on both metals and gold equities. If June CPI prints below 3.8% — plausible if collapsed crude oil below $69/bbl has transmitted to headline figures — the mechanism reverses: the hawkish minority loses credibility, hike odds compress, real yields fall, and gold can reclaim the momentum lost over the past six months. July 11-12 are non-trading days; Monday's print opens the week that determines whether Q3 2026 is a precious metals recovery or an extension of the correction.

headline: URANIUM FIRMS AT $85.75/LB — META, MICROSOFT NUCLEAR DEALS COLLIDE WITH CAMECO SUPPLY DISRUPTION AT $85/LB
snippet: Uranium held firm at $85.75 per pound on July 10, 2026 — up 19.5% year-over-year — as demand signals from AI hyperscalers converged with fresh supply disruptions: Meta signed agreements with Vistra, TerraPower, and Oklo to power its Prometheus AI supercluster in Ohio while the U.S. Department of Energy committed up to $80 billion for new domestic reactors, and General Matter received a $900 million DOE contract to build HALEU enrichment capacity. On the supply side, Cameco's Cigar Lake mine — the world's highest-grade uranium producer — operated under a temporary suspension starting July 1 after Orano's McClean Lake mill experienced an acid plant failure, a reminder of how fragile uranium supply chains remain at the margin. For uranium equity investors the structural case is intact: AI data centre power demand is adding a permanent new demand base to the nuclear fuel cycle at precisely the moment when Western utilities are racing to extend reactor lifetimes and governments are accelerating new-build approvals.

headline: BATTERY METALS REBOUNDED 143% — BUT THREE HEADWINDS CAP THE RALLY: EV SLOWDOWN, LFP CHEMISTRY, DRC/INDONESIA RISK
snippet: A July 2026 analysis from NAI 500 documents the sharp but structurally constrained battery metals recovery: lithium is up 143% from its 2024-2025 lows and cobalt and nickel have rebounded significantly, but three factors cap the upside. First, global EV sales growth collapsed to just 0.9% year-over-year in the first five months of 2026 (vs. 20% for full-year 2025), with North American sales falling 25% after elimination of U.S. tax credits and China contracting 15%. Second, lithium-iron-phosphate chemistry — now standard in grid storage batteries and half of China's auto market — contains neither cobalt nor nickel, limiting how much those metals benefit even as stationary storage grows (now 15% of battery demand). Third, the DRC has restricted cobalt exports since February 2025 and Indonesia uses quotas for nickel, meaning price evolution depends on unpredictable government decisions in producer jurisdictions. The rally to date has been supply-side forced braking, not demand recovery — and demand is running below expectations.

headline: CATL CLEARS FINAL SECURITY HURDLE TO RESTART JIANXIAWO LITHIUM MINE AFTER 10-MONTH SHUTDOWN
snippet: CATL, the world's largest battery manufacturer, has received security permit clearance to restore operations at its Jianxiawo lithium mine in China following a 10-month suspension — the latest in a concurrent wave of supply restarts that includes Mineral Resources restarting its Bald Hill mine in Western Australia (first spodumene concentrate expected July 2026) and Core Lithium resuming its Finniss project in the Northern Territory. The convergence of multiple major supply restarts is a key inflection signal for lithium price trajectory: the 143% recovery from 2024-2025 lows was partly driven by supply curtailment, and simultaneous restart decisions by major producers reveals that current prices are sufficient to justify operating costs — but also that the supply shortfall is actively being addressed. For lithium equity investors, Jianxiawo marks the pivot from supply-curtailment rally to demand-must-carry-the-load — and as NAI 500's headwinds analysis demonstrates, demand growth is running materially below prior-cycle expectations.
